s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with bilateral infiltrative shadows and fever following immunotherapy
salient_findings: New bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
key_facts: 82-year-old man with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma
Treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab
Follow-up chest CT showed new bilateral infiltrative shadows
Reported fever and dyspnea
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative
Serologic testing for various antibodies was negative
No history of antigen exposure
Received lascufloxacin and tazobactam/ceftolozane without improvement
Oxygen requirement increased to 2 L/min
Treated with methylprednisolone and prednisolone without improvement
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages
Transbronchial lung biopsy showed no malignancy
Cultures of bronchoscopy specimens were negative

shortlist.label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed bilateral infiltrative shadows and fever after immunotherapy with ipilimumab and nivolumab

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised due to cancer treatment, making opportunistic infections plausible

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised and has been treated with immunotherapy, increasing the risk of viral infections

shortlist.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe respiratory symptoms, including fever, dyspnea, and increased oxygen requirement

shortlist.label: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of exposure to various medications, including ipilimumab and nivolumab, which could trigger hypersensitivity reactions

raw.rationale: The patient was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab, and after developing new bilateral infiltrative shadows, was diagnosed with grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis based on clinical picture and imaging, and lack of response to antibiotics and presence of lymphocytosis in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: Sputum cultures and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative, and no other evidence of opportunistic infection was found

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
rejected.why: No evidence of viral infection was found, and serologic testing was negative

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient had respiratory symptoms, the clinical picture and imaging were more consistent with pneumonitis

rejected.label: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
rejected.why: No history of antigen exposure was reported, and serologic testing for various antibodies was negative
